case_number: Civil Appeal Nos. 9070-9071 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (Civil) Nos. 481-482 of 2019)

parties.respondent: Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation

summary: The appellant, a scrap dealer, suffered 70% permanent disability due to a bus accident caused by rash and negligent driving. The MACT initially awarded ₹15,76,465; the Delhi High Court enhanced it to ₹16,70,932. The appellant challenged the quantum of compensation, arguing under-assessment of loss of earning capacity (only 35% recognized despite 70% disability), inadequate future prospects, artificial limb costs, and pain & suffering. The Supreme Court examined whether permanent disability affects earning capacity, citing Sandeep Khanuja and Raj Kumar, and emphasized that loss of earning capacity must be assessed based on actual impact, not mechanically equated to medical disability.
legal_provisions_cited: Sandeep Khanuja Vs. Atul Dande and Anr.
Raj Kumar Vs Ajay Kumar and Anr.
final_judgment: Appeal allowed in part; quantum of compensation referred back to the High Court for reconsideration in accordance with the principles laid down.
